jars: My limbs give way, my mouth is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end (translation of Gita 1.30 is actually 'hair stands on end', but the app's translation says 'dry mouth' and 'trembles', which is a slight mistranslation)
The Gita opens with a panic attack, not a hero (this is a bit of a pop-psychology framing for a 52-year-old physician, though it works)
What you do next matters. Hold on to what is real in you (Day 4 - slightly preachy)
When a child leaves, a friend who shares the ache helps more than advice (Day 7 - a bit generic)
best: The Gita opens not with a hero, but with a man breaking down.
day1_verdict: Finally, someone understood the exact feeling of being suspended between a child who no longer needs me and a mother who is slipping away.
